neighbours.label: a phrase that re-specifies what was just said: 'in terms of', 'in the form of', 'what with', 'i.e.' (the other side of the - pole's 'including')
fire: The new law was a success in terms of public support.
These two cars are quite similar in terms of comfort.
We were always envious of them, what with their big house and pool.
The risk comes with real harm in the form of higher blood pressure.
Aid was promised to the region in the form of cheap loans.
Most large mammals, i.e. deer and elk, had left the valley.
They are tired, what with the long hours and the night shifts.
She studied the older texts, i.e. those copied before the fire.
quiet: The new law was a success with the wider public.
These two cars are quite similar and both are comfortable.
We were always envious of their big house and their pool.
The risk comes with real harm to your blood pressure.
Aid was promised to the region along with cheap loans.
Most large mammals such as deer and elk had left the valley.
They are tired after the long hours and the night shifts.
She studied the older texts and those copied before the fire.

notes: The - pole peaks on 'including', which adds examples; this pole seems to mark restating or specifying. Probe readings varied a lot for the same phrase (' terms' 0.14 to 0.67, ' form' 0.05 to 0.20), so this may fail on the median.
